description: We are a team of three passionate engineers and creators — Oleksandra, Hanna, and Mariia. For this challenge, we are developing a software solution to monitor and support astronauts' health and vital signs during long-duration space missions. Our focus is on combining intuitive UI/UX design, real-time data tracking, and reliable software architecture to ensure crew safety and well-being. We are dedicated to building a functional and impactful prototype!
summary:
Vital is our offline desktop app for Windows Surface. It monitors astronauts' health on deep-space missions. Because of 22-minute signal delays to Mars and solar power outages, Earth can't provide real-time medical help. So Vital runs a local "ship's doctor assistant" right on the crew's device.

It tracks 10 vital signs, from heart rate and SpO2 to radiation and bone density. If something's off, it explains why in plain language and suggests what to do. The activity log ensures the crew actually handles alerts — timed confirmations, erratic button-pressing checks, and inactivity detection. No fake taps.

Buddy-Guard lets the crew instantly see when a teammate is struggling, what's wrong, and how serious it is. They can rush to help immediately. It works via AES-256-GCM encrypted alerts shared between devices.

We also built a "blackout" mode with zero Earth comms to prove the system's autonomy in critical situations. Plus, MindCare tracks stress levels and guides cosmonauts through breathing and grounding exercises.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Vital is a local health-monitoring and decision-support app for a crew member on a long-duration mission. It shows 10 physiological indicators with norms and status, explains changes in plain language, recommends what to do next, and records what the astronaut actually did.

HOW IT WORKS

- Status and actions screen: indicators, norms, trends and prioritized recommendations in one place. Each recommendation is tied to a NASA HRP risk (cardiovascular adaptation, SANS, bone loss, radiation, sleep, behavioral health) with a link to the source.

- Activity journal: an action does not change the numbers instantly. The astronaut starts it, completes the real duration (for example 30 min of exercise), then confirms. Cancelled actions, rapid button-mashing, and long periods without any confirmed action while recommendations are pending are logged and included in the report for the flight surgeon.

- Buddy-Guard crew mesh: devices exchange heartbeats and alerts peer to peer. Packets are sealed with AES-256-GCM. If a teammate's vitals become critical or they raise SOS, the others are alerted.

- Blackout Vault: during a solar conjunction the app switches to autonomous mode, applies local safety protocols, and stores telemetry in a Merkle-delta log so it can be synchronized and verified when contact returns.

- MindCare: stress estimation from heart rate, HRV, hydration and sleep, with breathing, grounding and a one-tap SOS.

- Communication delay model for Moon, Mars and other locations, and CSV import of data in NASA OSDR format.

- Plain-text report export for the mission doctor.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Crews get immediate, explainable guidance when Earth cannot answer in time, and doctors on the ground get a verified record of what actually happened. It works without internet and keeps all health data on the device.

TOOLS AND REQUIREMENTS

Java 17+ and JavaFX, javax.crypto (AES-256-GCM), pure-Java expert system and trend engine. Runs on Windows 10/11, including Surface devices (x64, or ARM64 with a Java build for ARM64). Needs no internet connection, except to open the optional source pages in the built-in browser.

WHY IT IS CREATIVE

It treats the astronaut as a partner, not a data point: instead of a game-like interface it verifies real behaviour, and it combines health guidance, crew safety and blackout resilience in one offline tool.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Communication delay and blackouts, privacy of medical data, explainability over black-box AI, crew safety (peer alerts), and honesty: the app is a demonstration model, not a medical device, and its values are illustrative. NASA and CSA did not review or endorse it.

USE OF SUPER INTELLIGENCE

Parts of the code and text were created with the assistance of Claude (Anthropic), then reviewed and edited by our team. No images, video or audio were SI-generated.
